v.why: When the direct route only supplies blurred pooled features, a learnable 3x3 on the deep path contributes the missing spatial processing and gains more.
Without the input-to-output route the output depends entirely on internal paths, so upgrading the final deep edge matters more.
A strong conv on the other route into node 2 substitutes for the removed edge, so cutting edge 1 costs less.
A second near-identity path into the output pushes the cell toward shallow collapse, so the skip helps less or hurts more.
A residual is most valuable alongside a deep transformative conv path, giving the classic residual-block benefit.
Chaining convs along 0-1-2 compounds depth and receptive field, so the upstream conv gains more when the downstream edge also convolves.
A parallel conv into the output buffers the capacity lost by putting a parameter-free pool on edge 5, so the edit hurts less.
Conv capacity already supplied directly into the output saturates, so a second parallel 3x3 adds less.
If node 2's remaining input is only an identity copy of the cell input, removing edge 2 makes the 2-3 path shallow and hurts more.
With the deep path ending in identity, a pooled direct route leaves the output dominated by non-learnable signals, so the edit hurts more.
